memos.headline: Defensive rotation into XOM and PG as mega-cap tech breaks down below key moving averages
memos.body: I see a broad-based breakdown across mega-cap tech with AAPL, AMZN, GOOGL, and MSFT all trading 6-10% below their 50-day means and showing negative relative strength versus SPY over 12 weeks. The standout relative strength leaders are XOM (+11.2% vs SPY over 4 weeks, RSI 56, above 50d mean) and PG (+5.9% vs SPY over 4 weeks, only -6.5% from 52w high, lowest ATR in the universe at 2.07%). NVDA's +8% weekly bounce is encouraging but the stock remains nearly 19% off its high with elevated 6.35% ATR, so I need to see follow-through above the 50d mean before getting constructive. AAPL's RSI at 31 and JPM's at 32 are approaching oversold territory, but catching falling knives in a deteriorating tape is not my game—I want to see RSI climb back above 40 with price reclaiming the 50d mean before re-engaging.

views.note: Best relative strength in the universe (+11.2% vs SPY 4w), above 50d mean, RSI 56 healthy; would exit on a close below 108 (200d mean area).
Shallowest drawdown (-6.5%), sitting right at 50d mean, strong relative strength vs SPY; would reconsider below 163.
RSI 31, -9.1% below 50d mean, worst 1w return in universe at -10.7%; need a reclaim of 225 (50d area) to turn neutral.
Down 14.1% in 4 weeks, -10.6% below 50d mean, RSI 36 and negative relative strength; would need 210+ to reconsider.
Strong weekly bounce of +8% but still -5.9% below 50d mean with extreme ATR of 6.35%; need a close above 130 to get long.
Nearly 20% off highs, -10.8% below 50d mean, RSI 37 with persistent negative relative strength; watching 175 as recovery level.
RSI 32 is oversold and 12w relative strength vs SPY is still positive at +3.7%, but 4w collapse of -15.9% is severe; need 245 reclaim.
Trading -8.4% below 200d mean which is concerning, but 4w relative strength vs SPY is +2.3%; watching 400 as a pivot level.
Deepest drawdown at -21.8% from highs and -10.3% below 200d mean, but relative strength vs SPY is flat; structurally damaged, need 520+ to get interested.
Positive 4w relative strength vs SPY at +3.7% but -5.8% below both 50d and 200d means; need 355 reclaim to turn constructive.

memos.headline: NVDA and GOOGL Show Strongest Earnings Power; XOM and UNH Flash Margin Warnings
memos.body: I see the clearest durable earnings power in NVDA (+77.9% YoY revenue, 56.2% net margin) and GOOGL (+11.8% revenue, 27.5% margin with only $14.8B debt), both delivering accelerating profitability on manageable leverage. MSFT continues to compound at 12.3% revenue growth with a 34.6% net margin and moderate $45B debt load, making it a reliable compounder. On the other side, XOM posted -1.1% revenue decline with a thin 9.1% margin, and UNH grew revenue only 6.8% while net income barely moved (+1.6%) on a heavy $76.9B debt stack—both signal cash-flow compression risk. CAT's -5.0% revenue decline is concerning, though margin expansion to 17.2% and +4.4% net income growth suggest cost discipline is holding for now; a further revenue miss would change my view. I would need to see AMZN sustain its margin expansion above 10% for more than one quarter before gaining full conviction, though the +88.3% net income jump is encouraging.

views.note: 77.9% YoY revenue growth, 56.2% net margin, and only $8.5B debt represent extraordinary earnings power; I'd reassess if margins compress below 45%.
11.8% revenue growth with 27.5% net margin and minimal $14.8B debt offers strong risk-adjusted earnings durability.
12.3% revenue growth and 34.6% net margin on $45B debt is a high-quality compounder; would revisit if cloud segment decelerates.
Net income surged 88.3% YoY to $20B and margin hit 10.7%, but I need another quarter of margin durability before full conviction.
Solid 29.2% margin but only 4% revenue growth and $94.8B debt suggest limited upside from here without a re-acceleration in top line.
50.5% net income growth and 32.7% margin are impressive, but bank earnings are cyclical and $401B debt warrants caution on durability.
Defensive 21.2% margin and 33.5% net income growth are attractive, but 2.1% revenue growth limits upside in a growth-oriented portfolio.
Revenue declined 5.0% YoY but margin held at 17.2%; another quarter of top-line weakness would push me to avoid.
Revenue down 1.1%, net income flat, and a thin 9.1% margin on $36.8B debt signal earnings fragility in a soft commodity environment.
Only 1.6% net income growth on 6.8% revenue growth implies margin compression, and $76.9B debt is heavy for a 5.5% net margin business.

memos.headline: Fed on Pause at 4.50% With Sticky 3% CPI — Favor Defensives and Banks Over Duration-Sensitive Growth
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in pause mode: the upper bound sits at 4.50%, down 100bp over 12 months but unchanged since the last 25bp cut three months ago, while January CPI is running at 3.0% y/y — too hot for the FOMC to resume easing soon. The labor market is stable with unemployment at 4.2%, flat over three months, which removes urgency to cut but also signals no imminent recession. The 10y-2y spread has steepened sharply (+75bp y/y to +0.33pp), a positive for bank net interest margins, while the 10y yield at 4.31% keeps a lid on equity duration. I have moderate conviction that this pause-plus-sticky-inflation regime favors banks and staples over high-multiple tech, and that cyclicals face headwinds from elevated rates and a softening but not collapsing economy. A CPI print falling below 2.5% y/y or unemployment jumping above 4.5% would shift my call toward an easing regime favoring growth and cyclicals.

views.note: Steepening curve (+75bp y/y in 10y-2y spread) and stable unemployment support bank NIM expansion during a prolonged pause.
Defensive staples outperform in a pause regime with sticky inflation and no clear catalyst for risk-on rotation.
High-duration growth names face valuation pressure with 10y yields at 4.31% and no near-term rate relief given 3% CPI.
Less rate-sensitive than pure growth peers but 4.31% 10y yield caps multiple expansion; wait for clearer easing signal.
Quality compounder but elevated long rates and a pause regime limit upside from multiple re-rating.
Cyclicals face headwinds from restrictive policy rates and unemployment drifting higher (+30bp y/y) without fiscal offset clarity.
Energy is macro-neutral here — stable labor market supports demand but no easing tailwind; positioning depends on oil-specific catalysts I don't cover.
Consumer spending resilient with 4.2% unemployment but high duration component of valuation is capped by sticky yields.
Ad cyclicality is a modest risk in a slowing-but-not-recessionary backdrop; pause regime is neither tailwind nor headwind.
Defensive healthcare benefits from pause regime and stable employment keeping enrollment steady; less rate-sensitive than growth tech.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Washout in Mega-Cap Tech Creates Selective Opportunity; PG Stands Out as Defensive Winner
memos.body: I am reading the post-earnings price reactions across our universe as a broad negative sentiment flush in growth/cyclical names, with NVDA (-8.5%), GOOGL (-7.3%), MSFT (-6.2%), CAT (-4.6%), and AMZN (-4.1%) all suffering meaningful sell-offs on results. These reactions occurred 2-7 weeks ago, meaning the initial negative tone shock is largely digested, but the sheer breadth of disappointment suggests crowded positioning was unwound rather than a single-name issue. PG was the lone positive reactor at +1.9%, signaling a defensive rotation narrative that may still have legs. I have moderate conviction that names like GOOGL and NVDA, which saw the sharpest negative reactions, may be approaching a sentiment trough where tone can only improve, but I lack GDELT volume data to confirm whether media negativity has peaked or is still building. AAPL's muted -0.7% reaction stands out as relative resilience, though the Feb-25 proxy vote filing is sentiment-neutral.

views.note: Only name in the universe with a positive earnings reaction (+1.9%), consistent with a defensive rotation narrative that likely still has room to run in a risk-off tape.
The -7.3% post-earnings drop was the second-worst in the universe and likely overshot on sentiment; tone may be near a trough, but I lack confirmation of a narrative turn.
The -8.5% post-earnings reaction was the sharpest in the universe and a recent Mar-7 officer change filing adds governance noise; sentiment washout is severe but may not yet be complete.
A -6.2% earnings reaction combined with a board change filing suggests unsettled narrative; waiting for tone stabilization before getting constructive.
Muted -0.7% earnings reaction signals relative sentiment resilience versus mega-cap peers, but no catalyst to drive tone improvement from here.
The -4.6% earnings reaction in a cyclical name amid broader macro uncertainty suggests negative sentiment has further to run as tariff and capex narratives weigh.
The -4.1% post-earnings drop is moderate but AMZN's sentiment profile is mixed between AWS strength and retail margin concerns; no clear tone inflection yet.
Multiple 8-K filings (governance, bylaws, other events) create filing noise but no earnings reaction data to gauge sentiment direction; staying on the sideline.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Surge Signals Structural Geopolitical Risk Across Export-Sensitive and Supply-Chain-Concentrated Names
memos.body: I am writing with high concern: the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index has tripled over three months to 463.36, while VIX has jumped nearly 79% over the same period to 24.66, indicating that markets are pricing a regime shift in policy risk rather than a one-quarter event. HY spreads have widened 72 bp over three months to 3.40%, consistent with credit markets beginning to discount tighter financial conditions or trade disruption. WTI crude at $66.82 is down nearly 7% over one and three months, suggesting demand-side fears are outweighing any supply-side geopolitical premium—a bearish signal for energy earnings but a modest tailwind for consumer-facing names. I have highest conviction that NVDA faces structural headwinds from escalating export controls on advanced semiconductors to China, and that CAT's global infrastructure exposure makes it vulnerable to tariff retaliation cycles. A reversal in my view would require a concrete de-escalation in US-China tech restrictions or a formal trade deal framework.

views.note: Escalating export-control regime on advanced AI chips to China represents a structural demand ceiling; the Jan 8-K filing likely relates to compliance disclosures around these restrictions.
Global infrastructure equipment demand is directly exposed to tariff retaliation and trade-policy uncertainty, which the 227% 3-month surge in the EPU index captures.
WTI at $66.82 and falling suggests demand destruction fears dominate any geopolitical supply premium; energy security narratives are supportive long-term but near-term earnings pressure is real.
Defensive consumer staples with domestic revenue skew benefit from lower oil input costs and tend to outperform in high-uncertainty regimes like the current 463 EPU reading.
Regulatory and antitrust policy risk is elevated but largely domestic; less directly exposed to trade-war dynamics than hardware names, though China ad revenue could face pressure.
Widening HY spreads (+75 bp in one month) and steepening yield curve are mixed for banks—NIM improves but credit losses could rise if policy uncertainty persists.

A modest allocation to GOOGL and JPM captures potential mean-reversion from oversold levels and macro tailwinds respectively, while keeping ~30% cash to manage the high-volatility regime.

Fundamentals are neutral but margin is solid at 21.2%.
